html:
The African National Congress (ANC) is the South African movement that led the struggle against apartheid and has governed the country since 1994. It was founded in Bloemfontein on 8 January 1912 as the South African Native National Congress, two years after the Union of South Africa was formed.

Its first leaders, among them Sol Plaatje, were mission-educated men who petitioned and sent delegations to London, for example against the Natives Land Act of 1913. It sang Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika at its meetings from early on. It took its present name in 1923.

In the 1940s a Youth League including Nelson Mandela, Walter Sisulu and Oliver Tambo pushed for mass action. The ANC led the Defiance Campaign of 1952 and, with its allies, adopted the Freedom Charter in 1955. After the Sharpeville massacre in 1960 the government banned it. It turned to armed struggle through Umkhonto we Sizwe, and its leaders were jailed or went into exile.

It was unbanned in 1990 and won the first democratic election in 1994, with Mandela as president. It held a majority for thirty years, but corruption scandals and a failing economy wore down its support, and in 2024 it lost its majority and formed a coalition government.
